headline: Earthquakes release energy that has been building for centuries along fault lines
universal_truth: Tension that builds slowly can release suddenly and powerfully
fun_facts: There are about 500,000 detectable earthquakes per year; about 100,000 can be felt by humans
The largest recorded earthquake was magnitude 9.5 in Chile in 1960—it lasted 10 minutes
Earthquake waves can travel through the entire planet, revealing Earth's inner structure
discussion_questions: What tensions in your life might be building toward a sudden release?
How do you prepare for events you can't predict?
What can we learn from cultures that have lived with earthquakes for millennia?

hook.script: The ground feels solid, permanent, reliable. Then, without warning, it shakes. In seconds, everything stable becomes chaos. Earthquakes remind us that Earth's surface is just a thin skin floating on a restless interior. Today, we discover why the ground shakes.

cliff.script: Tectonic plates move only inches per year—about as fast as your fingernails grow. Something so slow should be gentle. So why do earthquakes release energy equivalent to nuclear explosions?

options.text: Friction locks plates together; stress builds for centuries until it releases suddenly
options.response: Yes. Decades or centuries of stored energy releases in seconds—that's what makes earthquakes devastating.

options.text: Underground explosions from magma create the shaking
options.response: Volcanic earthquakes exist, but most are from plate friction...

fact1.title: Plates in Motion
fact1.script: Earth's surface is broken into about 15 major tectonic plates floating on the mantle. They push together, pull apart, and slide past each other. Where they meet, friction locks them—until stress overcomes friction, and they lurch.

fact2.title: Centuries of Storage
fact2.script: Some fault lines store energy for centuries. The San Andreas Fault in California is overdue for a major release. The energy accumulates silently, invisibly, until the moment of sudden reckoning. Earthquakes are patient.

fact3.title: Waves Through Earth
fact3.script: Earthquake waves travel through the entire planet. By measuring how they bend and slow, scientists discovered Earth has a liquid outer core and solid inner core. Earthquakes are destructive—but also illuminating.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Tensions that build slowly can release suddenly. This is true for plates, for relationships, for societies. Pay attention to the friction accumulating in your life. Address it before it finds its own release.

outro.script: That's Day 53. Tomorrow, we'll discover how mountains are made. Until then, feel the ground beneath you—and know it's not as stable as it seems.

growTrack.title: Tension Audit - Where Is Friction Building?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify and address building tensions before they erupt
growTrack.activity: Where is friction building in your life? A relationship, a work situation, a personal struggle? Name it. Then ask: what small release could prevent a bigger rupture? Sometimes one difficult conversation prevents an explosion.
